questions.question: Give three reasons why Mansa Musa made his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324-1325.
questions.expected_answer: Religious duty (the hajj is a pillar of Islam); to display Mali's wealth and gain prestige in the Muslim world; to build diplomatic and trade links, especially with Egypt; to bring scholars, books and skilled people back to Mali.

questions.question: Explain the effect of Mansa Musa's visit on Cairo, and why historians treat some details of the pilgrimage with caution.
questions.expected_answer: He and his followers spent and gave away so much gold that its value in Cairo fell and had not recovered twelve years later, according to al-Umari; he even had to borrow money for the return. Caution: accounts were written years later by impressed writers relying on others' memories, so numbers such as the size of the caravan may be exaggerated.

questions.question: Describe the Djinguereber mosque: when it was built, by whom, its materials and how it is maintained.
questions.expected_answer: Built by order of Mansa Musa after his pilgrimage, completed about 1327, with design credited to al-Sahili from Granada. It is built of banco (sun-dried mud brick and mud plaster with straw), strengthened with limestone, with protruding toron palm-wood beams. It is replastered with mud by the community each year after the rainy season.
